`.rejects` and `.resolves` work on a promise, so you can pass the call itself to `expect`. An async function that only awaits that call rejects with the same error, and is more to read.

`--fix` replaces the function with the call.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```ts
import { expect, test } from "bun:test";

test("rejects an empty name", async () => {
  await expect(async () => {
    await saveUser({ name: "" });
  }).rejects.toThrow("name is required");

  await expect(async () => await saveUser({ name: "" })).rejects.toThrow();
});
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { expect, test } from "bun:test";

test("rejects an empty name", async () => {
  await expect(saveUser({ name: "" })).rejects.toThrow("name is required");
});
```

A function that does more than await one call is needed, and is not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { expect, test } from "bun:test";

test("rejects a second save", async () => {
  await expect(async () => {
    await saveUser({ name: "Ada" });
    await saveUser({ name: "Ada" });
  }).rejects.toThrow("name is taken");
});
```

## When not to use it

The two forms differ if the call can throw before it returns a promise. The async function turns that error into a rejection. Without the function, the error is thrown before `expect` runs.
